standard.title: Locate key information in texts and respond
standard.description: locate, with support, key information in spoken and written texts, and respond using gestures, images, words and modelled sentences
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can participate in classroom interactions and collaborative activities using modelled expressions (AC9LCH2C01, AC9LCH2C02). They can follow spoken instructions and respond through action. They have not yet systematically located and extracted key information from texts, made connections between text content and their own knowledge, or responded to texts with structured opinions or retelling.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students locate key information in familiar spoken and written texts with support, and respond using gestures, images, words and modelled sentences — including identifying main points, making personal connections, and expressing opinions about characters and storylines.

nodes.label: Identifying key words and main points in texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify key words and main points in familiar spoken and written texts, demonstrating understanding through gesture, image, ordering or brief response.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least three key words or one main point from a familiar spoken or written text, demonstrating understanding through gesture, image selection or spoken response.
nodes.typical_width: Listen to, read or view familiar texts and identify key words; demonstrate understanding of main points through sequencing pictures, creating captions, drawing scenes or responding to guided questions; use world knowledge to infer meaning of unfamiliar words from context.
wider: Identify key words and main points across different text types — spoken story, rhyme, cartoon, and written text — comparing how information is conveyed in each
Use knowledge of the world to infer the meaning of unfamiliar target language words in context, explaining the reasoning used
nodes.hinge_reason: Identifying key words and main points is the prerequisite for all text response work. Students who cannot locate information in a text cannot make personal connections, express opinions, or retell storylines — the higher-order demands of this descriptor and the creating strand.

response_modes.reason: Key word identification requires students to encounter a growing range of text types — stories, rhymes, songs, cartoons, informative texts — to build the reading and listening strategies that transfer across formats. Repeated exposure with varied texts builds this generalised comprehension capacity.

success_criteria: Identifies at least three key words from a familiar text when prompted
Demonstrates understanding of a main point through gesture, image, sequencing or spoken response

nodes.label: Making connections between texts and personal experience
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can make connections between text content and their own experience or world knowledge, and identify details about characters and events.
nodes.minimum_width: Make at least one personal connection to a text and identify at least one detail about a character or event from the text.
nodes.typical_width: Connect text content to personal experience and world knowledge; identify details about characters, settings and events in informative and imaginative texts; recognise that gestures and body language contribute to meaning in texts and in their own experience of communication.
wider: Compare the world of a familiar text (characters, settings, events) with personal experience — discuss what is similar, different or surprising
Identify examples from First Nations Australian communication contexts where gesture and body language carry meaning, connecting to how this also occurs in the target language

response_modes.reason: Making connections between text and experience requires scaffolded prompts — students at Y1-2 need explicit questioning frames (What does this remind you of? Who is like you in this story?) to move from comprehension to connection. Guided discussion and question supports develop this capacity before independent response.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background learners bring cultural knowledge and cross-language experience that enriches text connections. Width investment here — tasks that draw on students' bilingual and bicultural experience — produces richer responses and activates funds of knowledge that peers without background experience do not share.
success_criteria: Makes at least one explicit personal connection to a text, expressed in target language or English with target language key words
Identifies at least one detail about a character or event from a text

nodes.label: Expressing opinions and retelling
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can express a simple opinion about a character or text, and retell or summarise a storyline using modelled language.
nodes.minimum_width: Express at least one opinion about a character or story using a modelled sentence structure, and retell at least two key events in sequence.
nodes.typical_width: Express opinions about characters using modelled language with reasons; retell or summarise storylines after listening to, reading or viewing a text; identify a favourite character and justify the choice; use modelled exclamatory or evaluative expressions to respond to texts.
wider: Compare two characters or texts — what is the same, what is different, which do you prefer and why — using modelled comparison and opinion structures
Perform a scene from a familiar story, combining retelling with personal response and expression

response_modes.reason: Opinion expression and retelling integrate key word identification (node 1) and personal connection making (node 2) into productive response tasks. The teaching investment is in providing opinion and retelling frames that scaffold structure without eliminating personal choice — students decide what they think, the frame helps them say it.

success_criteria: Expresses at least one opinion about a character or text using a modelled sentence structure
Retells at least two key events from a text in correct sequence
